workflows.rationale: Per-head review locks and the exact-head carry-forward proof exist in the CodeRabbit adapter and the queue controller. Continuum's slot lock is the request-record comment rather than a label; the per-head property is the same.

Exact-head verdict binding, decisive-review supersession of nitpick-only COMMENTED reviews, status-as-operational-state, and a latest-state reconciler with full pre-write revalidation are all in the review adapter and queue controller. Loop prevention for generated release pull requests is retained through a trusted-automation policy rather than a status check.
A migration-era diagnostic that reads this consumer's own secret metadata. It is not a runtime parity surface and must not be adopted as production Continuum while its diagnostic use is still needed.

Product CI with a consumer-specific line-coverage threshold over the consumer's own sources. The generic half - a coverage threshold expressed as data and an exact-head blocking gate - is absorbed; the threshold value and the sources are the consumer's.

The global serialized quota controller exists in the queue controller with priority-first ordering and an in-flight timeout that releases a stale slot lock. Continuum's controller concurrency is now non-cancelling so a sleeping run is not reset by repeated wake-ups.

Canonical verdict parsing, prose verdicts, old marker compatibility and the no-retry-loop guards are absorbed by the adapter's reply parser and the review repair ladder. Continuum has one implementation where this file duplicates it in two workflows.
A migration readiness check that names this consumer's own secret and variable names. It is a cutover aid, not a runtime parity surface, and it is not part of production Continuum.
The bridge Continuum itself ships as a reference copy. It is the consumer's forwarding shim and must stay thin: no token, no permissions, no retry, no decision.

Priority ordering with deterministic tie-breaking, a bounded work-in-progress limit, lease reconciliation, attempt limits, blocked-by gating and a non-cancelling single global concurrency group are all generic scheduler semantics Continuum already reconciles from live state.
CI and packaging repair with a stale-lock age check, a lock released on every success, failure and abort path, and no persistent label that would suppress a later repair of the same head.

The agent lifecycle is generic, but the runner label is hard-coded here to a macOS image and the installer is retried inline. Continuum expresses both as configuration so the lifecycle stays generic and the execution capability stays a consumer choice.

Candidate, post-publish and canary production smoke for this consumer's packages, plus a production incident lifecycle expressed in this consumer's own channels. Continuum treats it as an exact-head blocking gate and a release-candidate artifact source, and creates no incident channel of its own.

A manual auxiliary reviewer outside the MVP orchestration contract. Retained in the consumer during cutover rather than deleted, because the issue of whether PR-Agent belongs in Continuum at all is separate from this audit.

Generated-file validation, the main wake-up, loop prevention and the trusted merge policy are generic, and the one specific rule is now ported too: a generated manifest is scanned for unfilled template tokens before anything downstream sees it, and a token named in a comment is read as documentation while a token on an active line refuses the build. See continuum.release.placeholders.

A serialized release lifecycle with a non-cancelling concurrency group is generic, and the recovery wake-up is now ported: a release-pr update deferred mid-publish is recorded as blocked rather than failed, and a terminal stage completing re-opens it by name with a wake keyed on the source head. See state.owed_reconciliation and ReleaseOutcome.reconciliation_wake.

Version identity, stable signing, publication and package-channel sync are absorbed by the release core and its adapters. Reuse of the exact bytes an upstream gate validated for the same immutable source head is not expressible: the journal records a manifest digest, never the artifact bytes or the gate that tested them.
Per-head review and repair lock reset on a new head. Continuum's equivalent is that a moved head settles the outstanding request record, so the slot is returned without any persistent label to clear.

open_pull_requests.rationale: Adds the shared engine build, static linking, a portability gate and a checkout hardening flag to three consumer-local workflows, and adds one new consumer-local workflow. No scheduler, review, repair, merge or release writer is added or restored, so it cannot reintroduce removed orchestration after cutover.
